newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T. shares tumble after US court ruling.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T. shares tumble after US court ruling.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T. Industries Plc tumbled on Friday in the wake of a Mississipi court ruling which sent U.S. tobacco stocks sharply lower.
B.A.T. shares dropped 31p to 523-1/2 by 0805 GMT, while shares in Imperial Tobacco Group Plc fell three pence to 435-1/2.
In the U.S., industry leaders like Philip Morris Cos Inc plummeted almost 10 percent.

The slide was sparked by a ruling by Mississippi's Supreme Court, which rejected a legal challenge to a suit to recover state funds spent treating people for smoking-related illnesses. The suit can now proceed.
It is the first of 22 such suits filed by state attorney generals across the U.S. to recoup Medicaid costs.
Analysts said Imperial Tobacco was unlikely to be much affected by the ruling as it is much less exposed to the U.S. litigation than B.A.T.
Nyren Scott-Malden, analyst at BZW, said he though the fall in tobacco shares had been overdone on both sides of the Atlantic, exaggerated by nervousness about the Dow's steep slide.
"It has been a gross over-reaction on the part of both the U.S. market and the UK market to news on a bad day," he said.
Scott-Malden said that after the knee-jerk fall, the shares should be able to recoup much of their losses. "But obviously markets are down and that doesn't help," he said.
